title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache - Peregrine Capital

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sofia Chen (Redwood CSM), Rajiv (CTO), Claire (Lead ML Eng), Omar (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Lena: ok hey everyone thanks for carving time today, we're gonna walk through Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix / kv cache and show some cost models tuned to the numbers you shared. quick check, is this still the latency-sensitive chat product for traders?
Claire: yes, low latency, p95 sub-200ms ideally, and we have a lot of repeated prefixes, trade confirmations, small prompts basically.
Rajiv: and security, we need VPC + KMS, also audit logs.
Lena: perfect, we'll touch on those at the end. Marco, want to kick off batching?

[00:02] Marco Diaz (SE): yeah sure, I'll share my screen — bear with me while I open the Optimize deck. so first principle: batching reduces per-token compute by amortizing attention / kernel overhead, but it increases latency unless you use continuous batching with latency budgets.

[00:30] Claire: can you define continuous batching again? we heard the term in the doc but want the mechanics.

[01:05] Marco: right, continuous batching is where the runtime holds short windows (e.g., 5-15ms) to gather tokens across concurrent requests, then issues a single kernel call. two knobs: max batch size and max batch wait. with dynamic windows, the system adapts to qps to keep p95 within SLO.

[02:10] Omar: so what's a typical setting for p95 200ms target?

[02:28] Marco: for that target and your traffic profile — short 20–50 token responses — we recommend max batch wait 10ms, max batch size 64, target concurrency shaping. That yields a 30–60% token-cost reduction in our experiments with similar workloads. caveat: if you have spikes above 1k concurrent, you may need Dedicated pools to keep latency predictable.

[04:00] Lena: switching to caching: two parts — prefix cache and KV cache. prefix cache means if the start of a conversation matches a cached key, we can reuse logits / KV cache up to a certain token length. KV cache is explicit key-value store for attention states used across prompt continuations. both help a lot for repetitive prompts.

[05:12] Claire: we have many repeated preambles and regulatory disclaimers — sounds like a good fit. how do you model hit rates?

[05:40] Marco: we ask for two inputs: unique prompt count per day and session reuse pattern. simple model: effective token-cost = base_token_cost * (1 - hit_rate) + cache_overhead. hit_rate we estimate from unique/total ratio. example: if 40% unique, hit_rate~60% on prefixes, you cut generation tokens by ~60% on cached prefixes.

[06:55] Rajiv: what's cache storage and eviction costs? and is it encrypted at rest?

[07:20] Marco: good q — storage is small relative to model compute, but eviction policy matters for hot keys. in Hosted we encrypt at rest using customer-managed KMS optional, in Dedicated / Private you can bring your own KMS or HSM. audit logs are captured per-request. we'll include details in the security pack.

[08:40] Claire: any gotchas with KV cache across different model variants (quantized vs fp16)?

[09:05] Marco: yes, cache compatibility is model-variant dependent — KV cache from a 4-bit quantized run is not always portable to an fp16 run. Optimize will recommend variant families and fallbacks. for aggressive cost saving we suggested a quantized variant for bulk inference and an fp16 or full-precision variant for low-latency critical paths with automatic fallback.

[10:40] Lena: bringing in cost numbers — here's a simple cost model with your profile. (Lena shares screen) assumptions: 200k prompts/day, avg response 35 tokens, 60% prefix hit rate from the sample histogram, hosted API pricing baseline $0.0008 per 1k tokens generation (example), Dedicated reserved pricing reduces compute unit cost by ~40% at commit.

[12:15] Claire: can you show delta with batching + cache?

[12:40] Marco: yes — baseline per-token cost ~X; with batching profile we reduce per-token by 30%; with prefix cache effective token generation drops by 60% so net cost reduction ~70% in the example. i won't promise exact numbers but the model spreadsheet we'll send has sensitivity knobs.

[14:00] Omar: is the 70% mostly from cache or batching?

[14:18] Marco: majority from cache (50–60%), batching adds incremental 20–30% depending on qps and response length. combined effects are multiplicative not strictly additive.

[16:05] Claire: what about tail latency impacts — batching sounds like it could hurt p99.

[16:30] Marco: absolutely — that's why we recommend latency budgeted continuous batching and hybrid pools. for p99-sensitive routes you can route to Dedicated low-latency pool with smaller batch windows and higher cost, while bulk user requests go to a background pool with aggressive batching. Redwood routing supports policy-based routing — by route or by token budget.

[18:00] Rajiv: could you run a benchmark that mimics our spike patterns? we have end-of-day surges.

[18:20] Lena: yes, we normally run a tailored benchmark on your staging with your prompt set and traffic emulator. Marco, will need sample prompt set and traffic hist.

[18:45] Marco: noted — we'll run 3 qps profiles (normal, peak, surge) and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost. we'll also test KV cache hit-rate scenarios: cold cache, warm cache, and hot keys.

[20:00] Claire: for Private deploys, how does KV cache placement work? local memcache vs external store?

[20:25] Marco: in Private you can colocate KV cache on the inference nodes for lowest latency or use a managed Redis layer with high throughput. tradeoff: local cache has fastest hit time but more memory per node; remote cache centralizes state and simplifies eviction. we can recommend sizes based on observed key cardinality.

[22:10] Omar: curious about consistent hashing if we scale out — cache affinity could lead to hot nodes.

[22:35] Marco: yes we use shard-aware routing and consistent hashing to reduce hot-shard problems; plus we recommend rebalancing windows and replica sets for hot keys. we'll include tuning guidance in the benchmark report.

[24:00] Lena: quick demo of Optimize Console — show the recommended batching profile, KV cache hit heatmap, cost slider. (shows a mock heatmap) you can simulate hit rates to see projected unit economics.

[26:30] Claire: can we import our telemetry to backfill hit-rate estimates?

[26:52] Marco: yes, you can upload an eventi export or we can pull from your S3 sample. simple CSV with prompt hash and timestamp is enough for initial modeling.

[28:12] Rajiv: security checklist — you mentioned KMS + audit. can you confirm SSO and RBAC for multiple teams?

[28:40] Sofia Chen (CSM): yes Redwood supports SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC groups. audit logs include token-level usage and API call traces; retention policy is configurable. we'll send the security pack with SOC2 cert and KMS integration docs.

[30:00] Claire: what about GDPR/data residency? we need EU-only for some traders.

[30:22] Lena: Hosted can pin regional regions; Dedicated/Private gives full control for on-prem or VPC-only. we'll list region options and data residency patterns in the docs.

[31:40] Omar: pricing question: if we do a Dedicated commit, do we still pay per-token for KV cache storage?

[32:05] Marco: storage is typically part of the Dedicated cost profile for in-cluster caches; for managed Redis there's small storage/network egress costs. the Dedicated commit lowers per-token compute cost substantially. we'll present 3 scenarios: Hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated 6-12 month commit, and Private license.

[34:00] Lena: showing a sample POC plan: 1) pilot week on staging to validate p95/p99 and cost, 2) canary on production for limited routes, 3) full rollout with routing policies and fallbacks. success criteria: p95 < 200ms on critical path, cost target X% less than current vendor.

[36:12] Claire: timeline wise, if we start benchmarking early April, when could we go to canary?

[36:30] Lena: typical 4–6 weeks: 1 week benchmark and tuning, 2 weeks canary, iterate — so potentially mid-May. depends on infra approvals.

[38:00] Rajiv: any reference customers in finance? we'd like to talk to a peer.

[38:20] Lena: yes, we have a couple of finance customers — i'll check permissions and make intros.

[39:10] Claire: minor point — you said quantized variant for cost. any accuracy regressions we should expect?

[39:35] Marco: small regressions sometimes for sensitive tasks; Optimize can run A/B with quality evals on your prompt set and surface regressions. for critical prompts we recommend running quality eval thresholds before routing to quantized variants.

[41:00] Omar: what about model rollouts and KV cache warming during a rollout?

[41:20] Marco: rollout policies can warm cache by seeding hot keys, or we can perform pre-warming traffic to build KV cache. when switching variants, Optimize supports warm-up windows and fallback to previous variant on regression.

[43:00] Lena: ok let's recap next steps. Marco will run the tailored benchmark once Claire/Rajiv share prompt set and traffic. Lena will send pricing and Dedicated sizing. Sofia will push security docs. we'll schedule a 30-min follow-up after benchmark results.

[44:30] Rajiv: thanks all — one thing, can you include sample scripts for the traffic emulator?

[44:50] Marco: yes, we'll include k6 scripts and a small python harness to replay timestamps and simulate spikes.

[46:00] Claire: timeline alignment — i'll try to get prompt set by next Monday.

[46:15] Lena: perfect. any last questions?

[46:40] Rajiv: just confirm that audit logs won't leak prompt content to third-party storage?

[47:00] Sofia: logs are stored in your region and can be configured to redact sensitive fields; we'll note the exact fields and retention options in the pack.

[48:20] Omar: small nit — in Private mode do we still get the Optimize console or is it local only?

[48:45] Marco: Private can run a local console instance or we can grant access to hosted console via your VPC peering; both supported depending on compliance needs.

[50:00] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and benchmark plan.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript with a few misrecognized tokens (e.g., "KV cash" sometimes appears), occasional speaker attribution errors. Full benchmark spreadsheet and security pack will be attached to the CRM note.
